findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=はらわた]腸をねじ切る苦しみ
findings.governingReading: agony that twists his intestines or guts apart
findings.explanation: The violent visceral pain is flattened into an ordinary stomachache.

findings.highlight: The man who turned away from the Einzberns
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=アインツベルン char=4]大切な人を切り捨てた男
findings.governingReading: the man who cast aside someone precious—read here as the Einzbern
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby, pluralizes it into the Einzbern family, and deletes Kiritsugu sacrificing a precious person.

findings.highlight: There was never a chance that Sakura could be saved
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を救う手段は、初めから何処にもなかった
findings.governingReading: From the beginning, no means of saving Sakura existed anywhere.
findings.explanation: The English turns the absence of any method into a probabilistic lack of chance.

findings.highlight: even if she’s going to obtain the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: あいつが聖杯を得るんなら
findings.governingReading: If Tohsaka is the one who obtains the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes a conditional outcome into Rin’s present intention.

findings.highlight: Rin will go mad unless she obtains the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を手に入れなければ崩壊する
findings.governingReading: Having killed Sakura, Rin will collapse or break down unless she obtains the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English specifically diagnoses insanity where Kirei predicts broader personal collapse.

findings.governingReading: kill Zouken, defeat Illya, drive Rin back, and destroy the Grail
findings.explanation: The English collapses distinct projected outcomes and says Shirou defeats Rin rather than repelling her.

findings.evidenceJa: 心を[ruby text=てつ]剣にしたまま
findings.governingReading: with his heart made into a sword, read as iron
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby material and deletes the written sword image that closes Shirou’s fatal commitment.
